questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a happier person in just a few simple steps
Why some countries are so happy, and if genes play a part
Why the weather in the north affects our mood so much
How the UN helps poor countries improve their economies
questions.why: Neil says they'll be discussing whether happiness is genetic, starting with the world happiness report.

questions.q: Which country came top in the UN's latest happiness report?
options: Denmark
Sweden
The UK
Norway
questions.why: Dan says Norway came top, overtaking Denmark, which led from 2012 to 2016.

questions.q: How are the results of the report decided?
options: 1,000 people in each country answer one question
Experts compare the wealth and health of each country
Doctors test thousands of people for depression
Governments send in their own scores every year
questions.why: They ask 1,000 people in each country a single subjective question using a 0–10 ladder.

questions.q: What is the average score of the Nordic countries?
options: About 5 out of 10
About 10 out of 10
Close to 7.5 out of 10
About 6 out of 10
questions.why: Dan says the Nordic countries all score an average close to 7.5 out of 10.

questions.q: What does Neil first guess might connect these happy countries?
options: Their food
Their long holidays
The weather
Their language
questions.why: Neil asks, 'There must be a connection… is it the weather?'

questions.q: What does Professor Andrew Oswald say about the Danes?
options: They have less of a genetic pattern linked to depression
They have the highest salaries in the world, on average
They are happier because of the cool, calm weather
They have more public holidays than anyone else in Europe
questions.why: He says the Danes have the smallest amount of a 'dangerous' genetic pattern, protecting them against depression.

questions.q: Why does Neil point out that Professor Oswald said 'in part'?
options: Because the professor made a mistake
Because only part of Denmark was studied
Because Neil disagrees with genetics completely
Because it means genes don't explain everything
questions.why: Neil says 'in part' means it doesn't explain everything, so something is missing.

questions.q: What is Michael Booth's view of why the Danes are happy?
options: It is mostly about their DNA and their genes
They are rich, funny and don't work very much
They live near the sea and spend time outdoors
They have very good free schools and hospitals
questions.why: He says the reasons have nothing to do with DNA: they're rich, sexy, funny and don't work much.
